headline: GOLD PLUNGES TO 7-WEEK LOW AS WASHINGTON REJECTS HORMUZ DEAL — FED HIKE ODDS SURGE TO 70%, BRENT ABOVE $106
snippet: Gold dropped to a seven-week low as the Strait of Hormuz standoff escalated: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the strait, pushing Brent crude above $106/barrel and reigniting inflation fears that sent market-implied odds of an October Fed rate hike from 51.5% to 70.3% overnight. Gold fell 3% to below $4,165/oz — extending September's 5.4% loss — while silver dropped 4.5% to approximately $61.88/oz. The mechanism is becoming a recurring pattern for junior mining investors: Hormuz disruption keeps oil elevated, oil keeps inflation alive, inflation gives the Fed cover to hike, and higher real yields suppress gold. With Chinese investors exiting ahead of Golden Week and GDX down 4.87% in a single session, the question heading into the October FOMC meeting is whether $4,100 holds as structural support.

headline: FIRST QUANTUM -31%: PANAMA COMMISSION RECOMMENDS ORDERLY CLOSURE OF COBRE PANAMA — ONE OF WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINES AT STAKE
snippet: First Quantum Minerals (TSX: FM) shares crashed as much as 31% on September 30 — trading from C$45.12 to as low as C$28.00 — after a Panamanian government commission recommended reopening Cobre Panama only in order to gradually and orderly close it. Cobre Panama is one of the world's largest copper mines (approximately 400,000 tonnes per year capacity) and was already shut since a 2023 Supreme Court ruling. The commission's recommendation, which stops well short of a full operational restart, crushed investor hopes for a return to production and underlines the political risk premium now permanently embedded in First Quantum's stock. Trading was halted for volatility before shares partially recovered to end down approximately 13%. For copper investors tracking supply-side risk, Cobre Panama joining Chile's Escondida and Centinela in simultaneous disruption mode is a significant Q4 supply shock being digested by a market already above $14,400/tonne.

headline: GOLD FIELDS WEIGHS ENHANCED BID AFTER NORTHERN STAR REJECTS A$38.7B TAKEOVER — DEAL WOULD CREATE WORLD'S #2 GOLD MINER AT 4.1MOZ
snippet: Gold Fields (NYSE: GFI) announced on September 29 it is reviewing an enhanced offer for Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) after the Australian miner's board unanimously rejected Gold Fields' initial A$38.7 billion (US$27.2B) proposal as 'materially undervaluing' the company. The original offer — 0.3125 new Gold Fields shares plus A$7.25 cash per Northern Star share — implied a 22% premium to the September 11 close and would have created the world's second-largest gold producer with roughly 4.1 million ounces of annual output and 77 million ounces of reserves. Gold Fields cited A$4–5 billion in risk-adjusted synergies, approximately half from tax reset benefits. The company confirmed it remains comfortable as a standalone but is contemplating a sweetened cash component. For junior mining investors, a contested mega-deal at this scale — the first go-hostile attempt in a major Australian gold M&A cycle — signals that record gold prices are generating the free cash flow needed to fund transformational acquisitions.

headline: ICG SILVER & GOLD DISCOVERS NEW HIGH-GRADE ZONE AT TUSCARORA, NEVADA: 24.3m @ 10.14 g/t Au INCLUDING 4.6m @ 51.84 g/t AND 1.5m @ 137 g/t
snippet: ICG Silver & Gold Ltd. (OTC: ICGSF) reported September 30 that drill hole T26RC-04 at the Battle Mountain target, Tuscarora District, Nevada, intersected 24.3 metres averaging 10.14 g/t gold and 3.4 g/t silver from 181.4 metres — a new high-grade gold zone not present in the existing 40,000-metre historical database. The headline interval includes 12.1 metres at 20.00 g/t Au, a sub-interval of 4.6 metres at 51.84 g/t Au and 10.2 g/t Ag, and a peak of 1.5 metres at 137.0 g/t Au and 25.7 g/t Ag. Phase 1 drilling totalled 3,000 metres; six additional holes await assay. The company plans to release an inaugural mineral resource estimate in Q1 2027, drawing on the full 40,000-metre historical dataset combined with Phase 1 results. For investors tracking Nevada gold-silver explorers, a 10+ g/t over 24+ metres in a new zone at only 181 metres depth — with visible gold at those grades — is the kind of intercept that re-rates market-cap-constrained OTC stocks before assays are even fully compiled.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY CORP FY2026: PRODUCTION UP 157% IN Q4, $93.13/LB REALIZED PRICE — HIGHEST AMONG ALL LISTED U.S. URANIUM PRODUCERS
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE American: UEC) reported fiscal year 2026 results on September 29 showing a transformational year: Q4 production from Christensen Ranch and Burke Hollow totalled 82,744 pounds — up 157% from Q3 — and the full-year weighted average realized price of $93.13 per pound is believed to be the highest among all publicly traded U.S. uranium producers. Full-year production was 229,294 pounds at a total cash cost of $34.24/lb, generating $37.3 million in revenue from 400,000 pounds sold. UEC ended the fiscal year with $753 million in liquid assets, zero debt, and two ISR mines operating in Wyoming and Texas — with a third (Ludeman) under construction. For junior uranium investors, UEC's combination of peer-leading realized pricing, a debt-free balance sheet above spot, and 40 drill rigs deployed at year-end is the benchmark against which other U.S. ISR developers are measured.

headline: GOLD MOUNTAIN IRAJUBA DRILL: 14.9m @ 3,520 ppm TOTAL RARE EARTHS, 43.5% MAGNET FRACTION — BRAZIL CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE ND-PR-DY-TB SYSTEM
snippet: Gold Mountain Ltd. (ASX: GMN) released October 1 drill results from five diamond holes at the Irajuba prospect within the Down Under Project in Brazil, confirming thick, near flat-lying, high-grade rare earth mineralisation. The highlight intersection returned 14.9 metres at 3,520 ppm total rare earth oxides (TREO) with a magnet rare earth oxide fraction of 40.8% MREO/TREO — rising to 12 metres at 4,051 ppm TREO at 42.0% MREO/TREO within it. A second zone returned 18.85 metres at 2,568 ppm TREO with a 44.7% MREO/TREO, with neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium averaging 570 ppm and peaking at 3,597 ppm. Length-weighted average MREO/TREO across all samples is 43.5% — well above the ~25–30% ratios typical for ionic clay REE deposits, indicating a commercially attractive magnet-heavy rare earth profile. For retail investors tracking Western rare earth supply chain alternatives, a high-MREO Brazilian ionic clay project advancing through drill confirmation represents exactly the upstream asset class that U.S. and EU defense procurement now needs.

headline: GDX -4.87%, GDXJ -5.15%, JUNIOR SILVER -4.96%: BEST MINERS TO BUY ON THIS OIL-FED October DIPS
snippet: Mining Stocks Today published a October 1 watchlist for the broad mining equity selloff: senior gold miners (GDX) fell 4.87%, junior gold miners (GDXJ) down 5.15%, silver miners (SIL) off 4.61%, junior silver (SILJ) down 4.96%, with copper miners (COPX) the relative outperformer at -1.46%. The author identifies three drivers — oil prices elevating Fed hike bets, Chinese investors liquidating ahead of Golden Week, and a stronger USD — and argues the structural bull market in precious metals is intact, with select junior gold and silver names now at price levels not seen since early Q3 2026. For retail investors deciding whether to add on this dip, the piece provides technical levels on Newmont, Agnico-Eagle and Franco-Nevada alongside mid-cap names where the leverage case is most compelling.

headline: TORQUE METALS PARIS GOLD CAMP: 70,000m DRILL PLAN, CHASING 1 MILLION OUNCES IN KALGOORLIE DISTRICT — 351,000 OZ RESOURCE AFTER JULY UPGRADE
snippet: Torque Metals (ASX: TOR) used its debut appearance at Mining Forum Americas on September 30 to present an ambitious 12-month drill plan of approximately 70,000 metres — with 20,000–25,000 metres allocated to resource definition — aimed at growing Paris toward the 1 million ounce threshold in the Kalgoorlie district of Western Australia. The July 2026 resource update already increased the project to 351,000 ounces at 3.1 g/t Au (up 67% from 2024), with the Paris deposit core at 2.01Mt at 3.8 g/t. September drilling at the Observation target returned 2.7 metres at 5.20 g/t gold from 201.2 metres (including 0.4m at 29.97 g/t), adding mineralisation below the existing 25,000-ounce Observation resource. For ASX junior gold investors, a sub-$100M market cap Kalgoorlie-district explorer with a clear path from 351,000 oz to seven figures and a BHP-scale infrastructure backdrop is a high-optionality setup heading into 2027 resource drilling.

headline: GOLD MINERS Q2 2026 SECTOR SCORECARD: BARRICK +50% NET EARNINGS, KINROSS FCF $726.8M, GREATLAND 80% MARGINS — RECORD CYCLE INTACT DESPITE PULLBACK
snippet: GoldSeek's quarterly gold miners fundamentals analysis for Q2 2026 finds the sector generating record cash at scale even as share prices pull back from H1 highs: Barrick Mining reported net earnings of $1.2 billion (up 50% year-over-year) with a 59% adjusted EBITDA margin; Kinross Gold's attributable free cash flow increased to $726.8 million; Greatland Gold achieved operating cash flow of AUD 406 million with all-in sustaining costs of AUD 2,196/oz and an approximately 80% gross margin; IAMGOLD generated $856.9 million in quarterly revenue at a $4,384/oz realized gold price. The analysis notes that while diesel cost inflation (oil above $100) is compressing margins at companies that set 2026 cost assumptions near $70/bbl oil, the high-gold-price environment has delivered record free cash flows that fund consolidation (as Gold Fields' Northern Star bid illustrates) and dividend growth. The Q2 fundamentals frame the current equity pullback as a leverage event — not a structural breakdown in miner profitability.

headline: MINING STOCKS CRASH TODAY: EXPERTS SAY HAWKISH FED FEARS DOMINATE BUT FUNDAMENTALS 'REMAIN STRONG' — ANGLOGOLD, AGNICO DOWN 40% FROM 2026 HIGHS
snippet: Canadian Mining Report canvassed mining sector analysts on October 1 as gold and silver equities took their worst single-day hit since May 2026: Anglogold Ashanti (AU) and Agnico-Eagle Mines (AEM) are both down approximately 40% from their 2026 highs, well into bear-market territory even as gold remains up roughly 8% year-on-year. Analysts broadly attributed the equity underperformance to three factors — a 10-year Treasury yield above 5.2%, October FOMC rate-hike odds now at 70%, and the Strait of Hormuz standoff compressing economic growth expectations while simultaneously feeding Fed hawkishness. The consensus view: the fundamental case for gold miners at record margins is intact, and the equity dislocation presents a Q4 entry window for investors with a 12–18-month horizon. The October FOMC meeting — whether hold or hike — is the next binary catalyst.
